title: Implement multi-timeframe candle builders with closed bar finalization
description:
Implement deterministic intraday candle aggregation in mike_trade/market_data/candles.py, with unit tests in tests/unit/test_candles.py.

Required behavior:
- Define an immutable Candle value type (a frozen dataclass or the equivalent). It carries: symbol; timeframe; start and end as timezone-aware UTC datetimes over a half-open interval [start, end); open, high, low, and close as Decimal; volume as Decimal; trade_count when known; source provenance (feed_id, a consolidated flag that is False for IEX, origin such as stream_trade/stream_bar/historical_rest/replay); price_basis (RAW or SPLIT_ADJUSTED); and status (DEVELOPING or CLOSED/final).
- Support at least the 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, and 60m timeframes through one builder. The builder accepts either trade ticks or completed 1-minute bars as input. Higher timeframes aggregate from 1-minute bars. Do not re-fetch anything.
- Bucket alignment is deterministic and anchored in America/New_York time. Callers can pass an optional session-open anchor (for example 09:30 ET), so that 60m buckets can align to the session open. Do not import the h.3 calendar module. The anchor is injected as a plain parameter or callable.
- Finalization: a bucket becomes CLOSED when an input with a timestamp >= its end arrives, or when an injected clock passes end plus a configurable grace period. Once closed, a candle is never mutated. A late event for an already-closed bucket is counted and reported as late. It does not alter the final candle.
- Provide a completed-bars-only accessor that never returns a DEVELOPING candle. Expose the developing candle only through a separate, explicitly named accessor.
- Fail closed on provenance or basis mixing. Feeding inputs with a different feed_id or price_basis into an existing series raises a typed error, or marks the series invalid with a reason. It never silently merges them.
- Reject invalid inputs with a typed error and no state change: negative or zero prices, negative volume, high < low, open/close outside [low, high], or naive datetimes.
- Keep bounded history per (symbol, timeframe) using a configurable maximum length. Do not use a raw tick archive.
- Do no network or provider I/O. All money and quantity values are Decimal.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/domain/market.py and mike_trade/domain/instruments.py (if present) for existing bar/quote/trade/feed types to reuse rather than duplicate
- mike_trade/market_data/ports.py, mike_trade/market_data/cache.py, and mike_trade/market_data/alpaca_stream.py (if present) for event and provenance field names
- mike_trade/backtest/clock.py (if present) for the injected clock protocol
acceptance_criteria: Candle is immutable: a test confirms that assigning to a field raises. All price and volume fields are Decimal, and start/end are tz-aware UTC.

A test feeds 1-minute bars from 09:30 to 09:40 ET and verifies the 5m candles [09:30,09:35) and [09:35,09:40). It checks exact OHLCV values, including the bar at exactly 09:35:00, which belongs to the second bucket.
A test confirms that the completed-bars-only accessor never returns the developing candle, before or after partial input within a bucket.

A test confirms that a bucket is finalized either by a later-bucket input or by the injected clock passing end plus grace, and that a late event for a closed bucket increments a late counter while leaving the closed candle unchanged.

A negative test confirms that adding an input with a different feed_id, or a different price_basis (RAW vs SPLIT_ADJUSTED), to an existing series is rejected or marks the series invalid. It is never merged.
Negative tests confirm that high < low, non-positive prices, negative volume, and naive datetimes are rejected without changing builder state.
A test confirms that per-series history is bounded by the configured maximum length.
IEX-sourced candles carry consolidated=False provenance, and a test asserts this.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
perform network, provider, or broker I/O
expose developing candles through the completed-bars accessor
use float for prices or volumes
run broad test suites or backtests
